title.narrative: EU as Guest of Honor at the Guadalajara International Book Fair (November /December 2023)

description.narrative:
The EU has accepted to participate as Guest of Honour (GoH) at the Guadalajara International Book Fair (FIL) at its November/December 2023 edition.

The EU participation as GoH will broaden cultural relations and encourage cooperation and co-creation between the EU, its MS, and the LAC region while supporting global circulation of European cultural works and artists; enhance the EU¿s role and relevance for LAC and globally, focusing particularly on youth (who make up most of the subcontinent¿s population); generate strategic public and cultural diplomacy actions that could be a template to reproduce and adapt to other global regions. The selection of writers, intellectuals and artists will represent the diversity (in geography, themes, and gender) and modernity of European literature/arts/thinking. Sustainable development, the green transition and climate change will be important themes. The regional dimension will involve stakeholders beyond Mexico, both internally (EU and MS representations in other LAC countries) and externally (artists, high-level speakers, etc.). Within the current circumstances of war, a powerful statement would be to display the larger ¿European family¿ by including non-EU European participants, such as Ukraine, Georgia, and Moldova.

title.narrative: Level of engagement online and on social media

description.narrative: Level of engagement online and on social media

comment.narrative: The figure totals 4604 visits on the dedicated EU web page 1705 Instagram new followers 272 Facebook new followers and 117 new Twitter X followers 5626 uses of dedicated hashtag. The dedicated webpage was the second most visited in 2023 in the ranking of similar events worldwide.From 15 November to 10 December the social networks of the EU Delegation to Mexico were dedicated almost exclusively to promoting the EUs participation at the FIL as Guest of Honour. It was done through different audiovisual materials and in close collaboration with the FIL which allowed for a much wider reach FIL registered 53 million impressions on its social media platforms. Communication colleagues at the FIL confirmed that the EU was the most active Guest of Honour on social media in FILs history.In this 25 days period we registered 1.5 million impressions 1.3 million accounts reached and 2094 new followers between our three social media accounts Instagram Facebook and Twitter. Instagram has become our best performing and fastest growing social network as it represented 80 of these figures allowing us to reach younger and more engaged audiences. Instagram 1705 new followers 58 own posts and 53 collaborative posts with the FIL 372 own stories and 47 reposted stories 1.2 million impressions 1 million of accounts reached. The amount invested on boosting some of our social media posts was around 585 PI budget.Facebook 272 new followers 58 own posts and 372 own stories 89 K impressions 87 K of accounts reached. No inversion on boosting posts.X Twitter 117 new followers 130 own posts and 84 reposts 168 K impressions. No inversion on boosting posts.Earlier this year we had two other successful monthlong social media campaigns. The first was in May in the framework of the Europe Month celebration which followed our tradition of dedicating one day to each Member State. This campaign titled Literary Month of Europe consisted of 19 videos of all EU Member States Ambassadors in Mexico recommending a bookauthor from their respective countries and 27 posts with interesting facts related to the literature of each Member State. The objective was to promote in the framework of the EUs participation as Guest of Honour in the 2023 FIL the great cultural and linguistic diversity of the EU among the Mexican audience particularly the youth. Then in AugustSeptember we had another campaign to promote some authors who would participate in the FIL highlighting at least one author from each EU Member State. It was an opportunity to start promoting some names and their most representative books. In the two weeks leading up to the FIL we had two additional shorter campaigns. The first was to promote the Literary Dialogues with Europe which would take place during the FIL and in which European writers would participate to discuss current issues in Europe and the world. The second campaign was to promote the evening shows that would take place every night during the FIL showcasing the diversity of artistic expressions that can be found in Europe.In addition taking advantage of the endofyear holiday period 16 December 7 January we published a series of new audiovisual materials 35 videos to look back at what was experienced at the FIL and thus continue to draw on the interest generated by this type of culturalsoftpower content.
